name: Mood-Congruent Memory
description: People more easily retrieve memories whose emotional tone matches their current mood. A sad mood can make negative material come to mind more readily, while a positive mood can surface more positive recollections.
design_relevance_note: Limited direct product-design relevance. It matters mainly in mental-health products, emotionally charged support flows, and retrospective research where a participant's current mood can skew what past experience details become easy to recall.
myth_risk_note: Faul & LaBar (2022) explicitly note mood-congruent memory is condition-sensitive and that mood-incongruent recall can occur, particularly under mood-repair conditions; Rusting & DeHart (2000) similarly find mood-incongruent retrieval emerges specifically during positive reappraisal. The effect is robust but not universal -- its strength and even direction depend on encoding elaboration, consolidation interval, and active mood-regulation strategies, consistent with the entry's existing partial status.
prevalence_note: Well established in affective-memory research and depression literature, but uncommon as a named concept in ordinary product-design practice outside specialist wellbeing or research-methods contexts.

findings.description: A meta-analysis of mood state-dependent memory research (1975-1985) found effect sizes vary systematically with methodological factors -- stronger with positive rather than negative moods, real-life (vs. laboratory) retrieval material, contrasting rather than neutral-baseline mood comparisons, longer mood-induction duration, smaller samples, and adult (vs. student/child) participants. Confirms mood-related memory effects are real but genuinely methodology-dependent, not a uniform, unconditional bias -- an honest complication rather than a clean universal confirmation.

A systematic review concluded that induced mood can bias memory toward affectively congruent material and autobiographical events, but the size and even direction of the effect depend on task conditions, materials, and mood-repair dynamics.
